questions.question:
Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Next, keep tapping the pot on all sides and at the bottom until the plant loosens.

B. Finally, slide the plant gently and remove the old potting mix on a newspaper.

C. The first thing to do when repotting is to remove the plant from the current pot.

D. Begin by holding the plant gently, and turning the pot sideways.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'CDAB'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In order to **arrange **such types of **jumbled sentences** in the correct sequence, we need to **follow **some **basic rules**.
 
• This **type of question** comes under the **chronological group category**.
 
• Just we need to **follow **the **words **like **first, second, next, last, finally, etc.**
 
• If we read the sentences, we get to know the **method of re-potting has been explained.**
 
• **Option C **must be the **first line **as it's already mentioned in the sentence. (The first thing to do)
 
• **Option D** will be the **second**, as it's explaining **how to start the process**. (Begin by holding)
 
• **Option A **is the **third **sentence, as it's mentioned **what to do next**. (Next, keep tapping)
 
• **Option B **is the **last **one, as the word '**finally**' clearly states the **last step**. (Finally, slide the plant gently).
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sometimes in the '**chronological group category**' sentence would be there **with the date or year** when a particular **event took place.**
 
• For example:
 
 
• In **1950**, he was born. In **1980 **wrote a novel. In **2010**, he died.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• In the given sentence, the **main focus** is on the **reason **to cancel the outing.
 
• **Reason **can be **expressed **with the words like **because or as**.
 
 
• **As **we were all busy that weekend we had to cancel the outing.
 
 
 
• The use of **notwithstanding **is **inappropriate **here.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Notwithstanding **(preposition) means '**despite the face or thing mentioned.'**

 
 
• **Notwithstanding **severe headache, he gave the presentation.
 
• Many criticisms **notwithstanding**, this movie broke the record.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

He drove the car very carefully on the hilly terrain.

options.text: The car is being driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.
The car was driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.
The car is driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.
The car has been driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The car was driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sentence **is in the **past tense (indefinite)** as the **second form of a verb (drove) **is used.
 
• To convert this sentence into passive, we need to make some changes.
 
• **Start **the sentence with **the object (the car).**
 
• **Helping verb (was) **with **3rd form of the main action verb (driven) **would be used.
 
• On the basis of the above-mentioned changes, the **passive sentence would be.**
 
 
• The car was driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's understand the concept with some **more examples.**

 
 
• He **bought **a costly mobile a week ago.

 
 
• *A costly mobile **was bought **by him a week ago. (Don't mention the doer if you want to draw attention on mobile only.)*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

“I love Bollywood music,” Deepu said to Reena.

options.text: Deepu had told Reena that he loved Bollywood music.
Deepu will say to Reena that he loved Bollywood music.
Deepu told Reena that he loved Bollywood music.
Deepu says to Reena that he loves Bollywood music.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Deepu told Reena that he loved Bollywood music.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sentence **is in the **past tense.**
 
• To **convert **from **direct into indirect speech**, we need to make some **required changes.**
 
 
• First of all, '**said to**' will be changed into '**told**'.
 
• Second, **remove inverted commas and use 'that'.**
 
• Based on the subject and object of reporting speech, bring some **changes in the reported speech noun.** *(Deepu is the one who loved music, so change 'I' into 'he'.)*
 
• Make required **changes in the verb based on the tense of** 'reporting speech'. ('**Said to**' represents **past indefinite tense **so the verb '**love**' will be changed into '**loved**'.)
 
 
 
• Now the **indirect speech would be**:
 
 
• Deepu told Reena that he loved Bollywood music.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Let's **understand **the same **concept **with some **more examples.**

 
 
• John **said to** Eva, "I__ **want **to be a great lawyer".

 __
 
• John **told **Eva that he__ **wanted **to be a great lawyer.
 
 
 
• Patrick **said to** me, "__I__ **like** Bollywood movies".
 __
 
• Patrick **told **me that he__ **liked B**ollywood movies.

questions.question:
In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

If you rent a house near your office, it will save your time as well as also money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'as well as also money'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If we observe the sentence, there is no need to use 'also' with 'as well as'.

 
• If you rent a house near your office, it will save your time as well as money.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**As well as **is an **adverb** that means **'also', 'too', or 'in addition.'** 

Normally, it is used at the end of the clause.

 
• We look forward to seeing you again and to meeting your wife **as well.**

**As well as **is a **multi-word preposition **which means **'in addition to'**.

 
• They have invited Robert **as well as** Jill.
 
• When I go to the hill station, I like waking **as well as** skiing.
